newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to cut industrial electricity tariffs.
newsitem.headline: Russia to cut industrial electricity tariffs.

text.p: Russia is to cut electricity tariffs for domestic industrial users who pay for their power supplies on time by up to 30 percent from July 1, Fuel and Energy Minister Boris Nemtsov said on Monday.

"A few hours ago, the Federal Energy Commission decided that from July 1, energy prices would be cut by up to 30 percent for industrial users, that is for those who pay on time," Nemtsov told reporters at a press briefing.
Electricity represents a major cost for Russian enterprises, especially in the power-guzzling aluminium industry.
The decision to cut electricity tariffs follows a similar government decision last week to cut prices for gas to domestic industrial users who pay off their debts to Russia's gas monopoly Gazprom.
Nemtsov, who is also a first deputy prime minister, is in charge of revamping Russia's so-called natural monopolies, including the gas and electricity sectors.
Russia's electricity market is dominated by Unified Energy System (UES). Gazprom and UES are Russia's two biggest companies by market capitalisation.
